To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C6 deficiency alleles arose independently on two C6 allelic back‐ground.
C6 haplotypes are associated with complement deficiency genes and with the RFLP at Msp I.
C6 deficiency in Caucasians and South African Cape Coloured populations is caused by mutations in two separate C6 genes, one giving rise to complete deficiency and the other to subtotal deficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular genetics of complement deficiency genes, in particular C6, and the association of polymorphic restriction sites with the C6 haplotypes.
the application of PCR to the study of the human complement system, and the use of this technology to the analysis of rare complement deficiencies.
the molecular genetic aspects of complement C6 deficiency, including a description of a new C6 gene polymorphism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Dde I B allele is the normal allele, whereas the Dde I allele is associated with complement deficiencies.
the C6 haplotype Dde I B‐positive, Msp I‐negative is associated with C6Q0 deficiency, whereas Dde I A‐positive, MSp I‐positive is associated with CSD.
the C6 haplotype C6A/Dde I‐negative/Msp I‐posi­tive is the most common haplotype in Caucasoids and Cape Coloureds, while the haplotype C5A/Dde I B/MsP I‐negative is the most common in Negroids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C6A allele is Dde I positive/Msp I positive and C6B is Dde I negative/Msp I negative.
C6 haplotypes are associated with complement deficiency genes and that the C6A and C6B alleles can be detected using PCR‐amplified DNA.
the Dde I/Mps I genotyping system is a valuable adjunct to the C6 charge phenotyping method for the study of C6‐deficient individuals and the investigation of C2‐C4‐C6 haplotypic associations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
C6 haplotypes can be used to identify the genetic backgrounds for complement deficiency.
C6 haplotypes can be used to determine the allelic basis of C6 deficiency.
the Dde I site in exon 2 of the human C6 gene is a useful marker for the C6 gene and that C6 haplotypes can be defined by the Dde I and Msp I polymorphisms.
